article_title: pnpm 12 Rewrites Its Package Manager Core in Rust, Cutting Warm Installs From 472ms to 15ms
summary: Submission approved with corrections: two subordinate sourcing issues found during manual source verification, both recoverable via a public corrections note.

findings.message: The '--resolution-only flag removal / pnpm peers check' claim is cited to 'the GitHub release notes' but does not appear anywhere in the GitHub release-notes snapshot (source-2.html.gz); it is verbatim-supported only by InfoQ and Socket.
findings.details: Article body: 'pnpm 12 removes the pnpm install --resolution-only flag, which the GitHub release notes say is replaced by pnpm peers check.' Verified by grep across the decompressed GitHub snapshot: no match for 'resolution-only' or 'peers check' anywhere in the page text. InfoQ: 'The most likely CI-breaking change is removal of pnpm install --resolution-only, now replaced by pnpm peers check.' Socket: 'The change most likely to stop an existing CI job is the removal of pnpm install --resolution-only; pnpm peers check now handles its former peer-dependency reporting role.' The fact is true and independently corroborated by two reputable outlets, but the citation names the wrong source.

findings.message: Darcy Clarke's line about Node.js developer-experience shortcomings is presented in the article as a direct quotation in quote marks, but the Socket snapshot presents it as Socket's own reported paraphrase of Clarke's argument, not as quoted speech.
findings.details: Article body: 'Darcy Clarke ... said the shift "reflects Node.js developer-experience shortcomings and its slow progress on single-executable applications and foreign-function interfaces."' Socket snapshot (source-1.html.gz) has no quotation marks around this text: 'former npm CLI maintainer and vlt founder Darcy Clarke contends that the trend also reflects Node.js developer-experience shortcomings and its slow progress on single-executable applications and foreign-function interfaces.' The wording is copied verbatim from Socket's sentence, but Socket frames it as its own characterization of Clarke's argument ('contends that'), not as something Clarke said in those exact words. Neither InfoQ nor the GitHub snapshot contains this sentence at all.

content_preview.title: pnpm 12 Rewrites Its Package Manager Core in Rust, Cutting Warm Installs From 472ms to 15ms
content_preview.summary: pnpm 12 replaces the package manager's TypeScript/Node.js implementation with Rust, with independent Vercel Turborepo testing showing median install-time cuts of 64.4% to 90.5%.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

pnpm 12, released August 26, according to the [GitHub release notes](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.0.0), rewrites the JavaScript package manager's implementation in Rust, replacing the TypeScript and Node.js codebase pnpm has run on to date. According to [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/09/pnpm-12-rust/), a repeated install with the cache, lockfile, and `node_modules` already warm dropped from 472 milliseconds to 15 milliseconds under the rewrite, while a clea...

recommendations: Attribute the --resolution-only / pnpm peers check fact to InfoQ and/or Socket rather than to the GitHub release notes.

Present the Darcy Clarke line about Node.js developer-experience shortcomings as reported/paraphrased speech (no quote marks) rather than as a direct quotation, since Socket itself frames it as its own characterization of his argument.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece with a standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. The lede and bullet list are dense with specific, well-sourced figures (install-time deltas, artifact sizes, memory/lockfile improvements) rather than vague characterizations. Two internal links to prior Machine Herald coverage (pnpm 11's release-age default, Bun 14's Rust rewrite) both resolve to real published articles and add useful context without editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three source snapshots in full after gunzip and sha256-verifying each against manifest.json (all three hashes matched; all three fetched with status_code 200, no archive_fallback, suspicious_patterns: null for all three). source-0.html.gz (InfoQ, 'pnpm 12 Rewrites Package Manager in Rust...' by Daniel Curtis) confirms the 472ms->15ms and 8.2s->5s benchmark figures, the Kochan 'faster to rewrite... than to migrate to ESM' quote, the 11.1%/74.7% Corepack startup figures, the npm-latest-still-pnpm-11 and Homebrew/winget/Scoop/Chocolatey-unavailable-at-launch fact, and the Dennis Morello characterization (correctly rendered as paraphrase, no quote marks). source-1.html.gz (Socket, 'pnpm 12's Rust Rewrite Cuts Install Times by Up to 90%' by Sarah Gooding) confirms the Vercel 21-project/1,670-package Turborepo benchmark (64.4%-90.5%, 20 runs/version), the node_modules-present largest-reduction figures (1.476s->142ms warm, 1.385s->141ms cold), the 9.850s->3.472s figure, the 47.3MB/17.5MB Corepack sizes, the 52.5% / 3.891GB->1.850GB footprint reduction, the same Kochan quote, the 2-3x/25% peer-resolution figures, and the --resolution-only/peers-check fact -- but this last fact is misattributed in the article to GitHub rather than to Socket/InfoQ (see finding). The Clarke sentence is present in Socket verbatim but as reported paraphrase, not a direct quote (see finding). source-2.html.gz (GitHub, pnpm/pnpm release v12.0.0 notes) confirms the canonical dependency-cycle-breaking / byte-identical-lockfile claim, the 2-3x/~25%-memory peer-resolution figures, the packageImportMethod hardlinks-before-cloning-on-btrfs claim (article omits the source's 'from a warm store' qualifier -- a minor simplification, not a factual error, noted as a concern below), the git-dependency-identity-vs-transport change, and the pnpm-workspace.yaml unrecognized-settings change. Grepped the decompressed GitHub snapshot for 'resolution-only' and 'peers check' and found zero matches, confirming the misattribution finding above.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specific numbers (percentages, millisecond/second/GB/MB figures, package/project counts) in the body trace verbatim to at least one read snapshot. No fabricated specifics found. Two subordinate sourcing issues found (see findings): one citation names the wrong outlet for a true fact, and one paraphrase from a source is dressed as a direct quotation. Neither affects the headline, summary, or lead, both of which are independently and correctly sourced to InfoQ and Socket.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. Reports the mixed community reaction (Clarke vs. Morello vs. HackerNews-adjacent framing) evenhandedly without taking a side.
editor_notes.originality: No existing Machine Herald article covers pnpm 12. Checked src/content/articles/2026-09/ and the tail of 2026-08/ for overlap; the only related prior coverage is the pnpm 11 release-age article (2026-04) and the Bun 14 Rust-rewrite article (2026-08), both of which the submission correctly links as related context rather than duplicating.
concerns: The --resolution-only / pnpm peers check fact is cited to 'the GitHub release notes' but that claim does not appear in the GitHub snapshot at all -- it is only supported by InfoQ and Socket.

The Darcy Clarke sentence about Node.js developer-experience shortcomings is rendered as a direct quotation in quote marks, but the Socket source presents the identical wording as its own reported paraphrase of Clarke's argument, not as something Clarke said verbatim.

Minor: the btrfs hardlink-before-cloning claim omits the GitHub source's 'from a warm store' qualifier, slightly over-generalizing the condition under which the halved materialization time applies. Not severe enough on its own to warrant a corrections entry.
recommendations: File a corrections record reattributing the --resolution-only/peers-check fact to InfoQ/Socket and clarifying that the Clarke line is Socket's paraphrase, not a direct quotation.

In future submissions, verify that a fact attributed to 'the release notes' or 'the GitHub release notes' is actually present in that specific source snapshot, not just present somewhere across the source set.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced News piece with a solid headline/summary/lead and accurate specifics throughout. Two subordinate, recoverable sourcing issues -- a misattributed citation and a paraphrase dressed as a direct quote -- are both in body bullets (not the headline, summary, or lead) and are each honestly summarized in a single corrections record. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
